class.name: PNCCProcessor
class.brief_description: Implements a Power-Normalized Cepstral Coefficients (PNCC) feature extractor.
class.description: Extracts Power-Normalized Cepstral Coefficients (PNCC) from an audio signal, a feature representation similar to MFCC but more robust to noise and reverberation, commonly used as a front-end for speech and keyword recognition. It can be used with [DTWMatcher] for keyword spotting.

method.name: compute
method.description: Computes the PNCC features for the given audio samples. The samples are expected to be a 1D [PackedFloat32Array] each value in [code][-1.0, 1.0][/code]. The output is a 2D array ([Array] of [PackedFloat32Array]) where each row is a frame and each column is a coefficient.

members.member: The length of each frame in samples, a longer frame length will give more frequency resolution but less time resolution.
The number of samples between the start of each frame. A smaller hop length will give more time resolution but less frequency resolution.
The noise floor's rise rate, a higher lambda_a will preserve speech onsets better but adapt more slowly to rising noise.
The noise floor's fall rate, a higher lambda_b will keep the floor elevated longer after loud segments but suppress noise less aggressively in quiet stretches.
The masking peak's decay rate, a higher lambda_t will extend forward masking over more frames but reduce fine temporal detail.
The half-width of the medium-time averaging window in frames, a higher medium_time_frames will smooth the power trajectory more but reduce responsiveness to fast changes.
The number of DCT coefficients kept per frame. The more coefficients, the more information is captured, but it will also be more sensitive to noise.
The number of gamma frequency bands to use. The more bands, the more information is captured, but it will also be more sensitive to noise.
The exponent for the power law transformation. This controls the non-linearity of the transformation.
The sample rate of the audio signal in Hz. This should match the sample rate of the input audio.
